subject: Re: Next steps: PoC deployment mode & trial plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Turner <sasha.turner@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: deployment modes & PoC success criteria

Hi Sasha —

Great to meet you and the team today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can scope a tight PoC: 

Summary of options we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to start, pay-as-you-go, Redwood-managed model updates. Good if you want minimal infra and fastest time to value.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; customer data isolation from multi-tenant pools.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed network, required for regulated data or air-gapped needs.

Questions we need to finalize PoC scope:
1) Primary success criteria (latency target, throughput, accuracy/regression metrics, cost baseline)?
2) Which deployment mode should we validate first (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)? If you need a decision tree, we can propose one based on compliance and traffic profile.
3) Stakeholders & timelines: who from your infra/security/procurement teams should be looped in and target date for PoC start?
4) Any mandatory security artifacts (SOC2, network diagrams, data retention policies) we should attach up front?

Proposed PoC plan (high level):
- Week 0: kickoff + access & success criteria alignment
- Week 1-2: test dataset ingest & baseline runs (Hosted or Dedicated)
- Week 3: scale tests + latency profiling, evaluate caching/batching
- Week 4: handoff + recommendations / next-step pricing

Attached is a draft PoC plan that maps milestones to owners and a placeholder timeline. If Hosted is acceptable we can spin this up in 48-72 hours; Dedicated needs instance sizing and a slightly longer lead (2-3 weeks scheduling), and Private/VPC/on-prem will require security intake and network setup (3-6+ weeks depending on approvals).

Attachment: Redwood_PoC_plan.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

If you can confirm the success criteria and preferred deployment mode, I’ll update the plan and loop in Marissa (our Solutions lead) and Jordan (support/ops) for technical alignment.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

---
From: Sasha Turner <sasha.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lee Chen <lee.chen@acme-corp.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment modes & PoC success criteria

Thanks Ben — good summary. A few clarifying notes from our side after internal sync: 

Success criteria (priority order):
1) Latency: 95th percentile request latency under 300ms for 512-token context for assistant-style prompts.
2) Throughput: sustain 300 req/min with bursts to 600 for 5-10 minutes.
3) Accuracy/regression: parity or better vs our existing baseline prompts (we have ~50 eval prompts).
4) Cost: monthly spend target (TBD) but we want visibility into per-token cost and suggestions to optimize.

Deployment preference:
- Prefer Dedicated capacity if Redwood can provide predictable latency and lower unit cost. We are open to Hosted for initial small-scale validation if Dedicated scheduling takes too long, but Private/VPC is likely not required for phase 1 (we're cloud-first and not air-gapped).

Stakeholders:
- Sasha Turner (owner, product)
- Lee Chen (DevOps lead) - will own infra validation
- Procurement (procurement@acme-corp.com) - will be involved once we agree on commercial terms
- Security (I'll introduce if we go Private/VPC)

Timeline: target PoC kickoff week of Mar 9, 2026. If you can start a Hosted pilot sooner, we could run a 2-week smoke before then.

Also attaching our minimal privacy/data handling notes and a short list of prompts for the eval.

Thanks,
Sasha

Attachment: Acme_PoC_prompts.txt (TXT, 4KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Turner <sasha.turner@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment modes & PoC success criteria

Perfect - thanks for the clarity, Sasha. Based on your priorities I propose the following pragmatic two-track approach so we can hit your Mar 9 target while validating Dedicated requirements: 

1) Quick Hosted smoke (optional, 48-72 hours):
- Purpose: validate accuracy and baseline latency on your eval prompts with minimal setup.
- Deliverables: baseline report, token/cost estimate, any prompt fixes.

2) Dedicated PoC (primary track):
- Start: aim to begin Dedicated provisioning the week of Mar 9. We'll size the reserved pool for 2x your expected throughput (to handle bursts) and run the same evals plus scale testing.
- Timeline: provisioning (2 weeks), run (2-3 weeks), analysis (1 week) - total 5-6 weeks from provisioning.
- Success criteria: meeting the latency & throughput targets above and acceptable cost per token.

Next actions for us:
- I'll update the PoC plan and MPA (mutual action plan) and send an updated timeline.
- Jordan, can you prepare the initial Dedicated sizing options and any infra prerequisites we should share with Lee?
- Sasha, please confirm if Hosted smoke is useful; if so we'll queue it this week.

Attachment: Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

Jordan (cc) - tagging you to own the Dedicated sizing and to coordinate with Lee on network/whitelisting if needed. Marissa, I’ve looped you to handle success criteria tracking and the security questionnaire handoff.

Best,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Turner <sasha.turner@acme-corp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment modes & PoC success criteria

Hi all - looping in a couple quick operational notes from the Solutions team so expectations are clear on the security/compliance side: 

- If you decide to proceed with Dedicated, please expect a short security intake: we'll need a network diagram and confirmation of IPs for allowlisting, and a brief questionnaire (SOC2 items). I attached a stub of the SOC2 evidence we can provide immediately.
- For Hosted pilot we'll provide token-level cost breakdowns and tracing hooks; you'll get a short runbook for ingest and eval collection.
- I’ll set up a kickoff with our performance engineer (Jordan) and your DevOps (Lee) to finalize load profile and sampling for the 50 eval prompts.

Proposed meeting times (PT): Wed Mar 4 10:00am or Thu Mar 5 2:00pm - which works for you, Sasha?

Attachment: SOC2_evidence_stub.txt (TXT, 6KB)

Thanks - I’ll also add these milestones to the MPA and share an updated version after Ben’s edits.

-Marissa
